newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Boots says card to boost spending.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Boots says card to boost spending.

text.p: British retailer Boots Co Plc said on Wednesday it expected the nationwide launch of its Advantage loyalty card could raise the average amount spent in a Boots The Chemist store by about one third.
Steve Russell, managing director of Boots The Chemists said the average spending in a Boots store was currently 6.11 stg per customer.
But regional trials of the card in East Anglia and the south west of England showed the card did increase shoppers' average spending when they visited the store.
"I think the average spend on the Advantage card is about 30 percent higher," he told Reuters by telephone.

Boots predicted its Advantage card, due to be available from September 1, would deliver a four percent uplift in sales by the end of the 1998/99 financial year. Boots The Chemists' sales last year were 3.3 billion stg.
Phil Douty, head of customer communications, estimated the sales boost would translate into gross profit of 109 million stg.
"Over the three-year period the gross profit accruing from the incremental sales is 109 million pounds.....before all the expenses," he said.
The company said the card would pay for itself by the end of the next financial year and Boots would have recovered its investment costs as well as the operating costs on the scheme.
Russell said although Boots' customers were already loyal, the card would encourage them either to visit the shops more regularly or buy more items at slightly higher prices.
"There are also some customers where we don't have as much loyalty as we would like and we're pulling them into the net," he said.
The card carries a computer chip, giving Boots the capacity to compile a detailed database from purchases made by individual customers.
"The prime benefit is that we are now able to put a name against the...store receipts," Douty said.
He said this would be valuable for evaluating product launches and the impact of new marketing campaigns.
Boots' scheme follows a wave of loyalty card programmes introduced after supermarket group Tesco Plc's launched its highly successful Clubcard. -- Jane Merriman, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
